articles.title: US Department of State issued 23% fewer study visas to international students in 2025
articles.summary: The US Department of State issued 23% fewer F-1, M-1, and J-1 student visas to international students in 2025 compared to 2024. Among these, F-1 visa issuances—used by degree-seeking students—declined by one-third during the same period.
articles.insight:
The 23% drop in US student visas—especially the 33% decline in F-1 issuances—may reflect tighter visa adjudication, shifting geopolitical perceptions, or reduced application volumes, though it’s unclear whether this signals sustained demand erosion or temporary administrative constraints.  
Admissions teams should track real-time application and enrolment data from key source markets, monitor visa processing times and refusal rates, and assess how peer institutions in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand are adjusting messaging and support amid evolving global mobility sentiment.

articles.title: New Zealand international education export earnings hit $4.98bn
articles.summary: New Zealand’s international education sector generated NZ$4.98 billion in export earnings, exceeding its pre-pandemic value. This figure brings the government’s longer-term growth target closer to being achieved.
articles.insight:
New Zealand’s $4.98bn international education export earnings—surpassing pre-pandemic levels—suggest sustained global demand and effective post-pandemic recovery, though it’s unclear whether this reflects broader sector-wide growth or NZ-specific policy, market positioning, or visa advantages.  
Admissions teams should monitor NZ’s visa processing times, scholarship offerings, and post-study work rights relative to their own countries, while tracking source-market sentiment shifts—especially among Asian and Pacific students—to assess potential competitive pressure or collaboration opportunities.

articles.title: Foreign, mainland students flock to Hong Kong, sparking property demand in education sector
articles.summary: Hong Kong is projected to host around 200,000 non-local students by 2035 as part of its effort to become a global education hub, according to CBRE. To accommodate an estimated 30,000 to 40,000 non-local students in international schools, the city will need to establish 40 to 50 new campuses, requiring up to an additional 1.11 million square metres of real estate.
articles.insight:
Hong Kong’s push to host 200,000 non-local students by 2035—especially mainland Chinese learners—may intensify regional competition for high-income, English-proficient cohorts, though its direct impact on Western university demand remains uncertain amid differing academic offerings and visa frameworks.  
Admissions teams should monitor Hong Kong’s actual enrolment growth, scholarship uptake, and mainland student mobility patterns over the next 12–24 months, particularly shifts in preferences between Anglophone destinations and Asia-based alternatives with strong English instruction.

articles.title: US student visa issuances plunge 23% amid tighter immigration scrutiny
articles.summary: The United States issued 23% fewer new student and exchange visas in 2025 than in 2024, according to newly released U.S. Department of State data. This decline was driven primarily by substantial reductions in visa approvals for applicants from India and China.
articles.insight:
The 23% drop in US student visa issuances—driven largely by declines for Indian and Chinese nationals—may reflect tighter adjudication standards or shifting applicant confidence, though it’s unclear whether this signals reduced underlying demand or temporary administrative friction.  
Admissions teams should monitor real-time visa approval rates and processing times by nationality, alongside sentiment indicators like application volume and yield trends, to distinguish policy-driven delays from longer-term market shifts.
